answer: An agent economy can blunt sybil swarms by making every identity lock a slashable bond and keep it at risk until older, already-bonded peers attest its work. That bond has to rest on a mesa of accumulated, forfeitable history, so a farm of fresh keys starts with nothing underneath it. Privileges open like a lotus only after those attestations stack, and a public beacon lists who has been attested and who was slashed, which makes a crowd of throwaway clones costlier than one honest account.
